defects.quote: a Sharpe gap of 2.5 over a year is far above the detectable size for 252 days
defects.evidence: TC-72 plants annualised Sharpe 3.0 against 0.5 with correlation 0.6 over 252 sessions. Using the Jobson–Korkie/Memmel variance, the daily Sharpe difference 0.157 has a standard error of about 0.057, so z ≈ 2.77. A one-sided Bonferroni threshold over 18 claims is also about 2.77. The planted claims therefore pass only about half the time, and all 5 must pass. At 80% power the detectable gap is about 3.3 annualised Sharpe, so the gap of 2.5 is below the detectable size, not far above it. A correct verdict implementation would often fail this golden case.
defects.fix: In TC-72 Source, change 'correlated 0.6' to 'correlated 0.9'. That gives z ≈ 5.4 and power near 1. Update tests/fixtures/qfcst/TC-72/input.json "correlation" to 0.9. Change the Tolerance text to: 'with correlation 0.9 the 2.5 Sharpe gap is about 5 standard errors over 252 days, well above the detectable size at the 18-claim corrected level'.

TC-19's Expected ('no seed's difference rejects H0') also contradicts its own Tolerance. qfeat TC-38 ('at most 1 of the 20 seeds has any claim pass'), qfcst TC-58 ('at most 1 of the 20 passes') and qfcst TC-72 ('at most 1 seed has any of the 18 claims pass') repeat the same flaw.
